recipes.name: Spicy Coconut and Lime Grilled Shrimp
ingredients_raw: 1 pound uncooked medium shrimp, peeled and deveined
bamboo skewers, soaked in water for 30 minutes

steps.text: Combine jalapeños, lime zest, lime juice, and garlic in a blender. Add cilantro, coconut, oil, and soy sauce; blend until smooth.
Place shrimp in a large glass or ceramic bowl. Pour in marinade and toss to evenly coat. Cover with plastic wrap and marinate in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours.
Preheat an outdoor grill for medium-high heat and lightly oil the grate.
Remove shrimp from marinade and gently shake off excess. Discard remaining marinade.
Thread shrimp onto skewers, piercing each shrimp near the head and tail.
Place skewers onto the preheated grill; cook until nicely browned on all sides and the meat is opaque, 2 to 3 minutes per side.

raw_recipe.headline: Spicy Coconut and Lime Grilled Shrimp
raw_recipe.description: This easy coconut lime shrimp recipe with a touch of spice from jalapeño peppers is a perfect appetizer for summer cookouts.

review.reviewBody: Let me tell you... I never, I mean NEVER ever want to eat any other kind of shrimp other than these again! OMG! They are utterly delicious! I did change it slightly... I was having a party consisting of 50+ people coming so I had to up the quantities. Upon reading other reviews, I made the following changes... I used 6 pounds of shrimp, 9 jalapenos, 5 large lime (just the juice, I guess in my rush, I didn't remember to zest them), 7 heaping tablespoons minced garlic, 2 cups fresh cilantro, 2 cups sweetened shredded coconut, 1 cup oil & 1 cup soy sauce. I also added one can of coconut milk to the mix. Zipped everything through my food processor and marinated the shrimp for 3-4 hours. My marinade was not thick but it was chunky and when I skewered them, I made sure I didn't shake anything off of them, so what stuck to the shrimp stayed on the shrimp. Hubby grilled them up and these were cleared out in no time at all! Even my husbands family who usually doesn't comment on the food was asking what was in them! That tells me something... Yum! I can't wait to eat these again!

I made the marinade the night before . The jalapeños didn't have much heat, so I added 1/4 tsp. cayenne. Based on the reviews, I also added about 1/4 cup coconut milk and added a couple of hefty tablespoons in mayo for a dipping sauce. I marinated the shrimp the next morning for a few hours, and my husband grilled over low heat. They were really, really good. No one tasted any coconut (despite the coconut milk). The primary flavors were cilantro and jalapeño (the pepper, not the heat since they were seeded and not too spicy in the first place). While I'd be tempted to omit the coconut, I think it probably adds something, maybe sweetness? So I won't. This is really easy to make, and I can't wait to try it on other stuff -- fish, chicken, scallops.

Loved these shrimps! Used fresh coconut and coconut milk. Wrapped shrimp in bacon (half a thin slice), and deep fried for 3 minutes at 350°.Set aside about 1/3 cup of marinade and mixed with mayo for dipping sauce. That made the dish!
Very delicious....I only added 1 jalapeño and put it in a ziploc bag as the marinade is very chunky and the first time I made it from a bowl not everything was coated! Amazing recipe!

oh my this was amazing! i came across this while looking for ideas to make dinner with cilantro and lime as my key components and wanted shrimp. this definitely caught my eye and now it's been put into my favorites.
i did make the following changes - i increased all liquids slightly as i was making double the shrimp. instead of jalepeno, i used anaheim peppers (didn't want it too spicy). and since i live in an apartment, i don't have a grill, so i just cooked them in my large skillet. (i may consider using coconut milk as some did for more of that coconut flavor).
the shrimp were tender and juicy and the sauce from the marinade was perfectly flavored. i did garnish with a little chopped cilantro mixed with a little of the coconut. 
thank you for providing the inspiration for my dinner!!

Really, really loved this and since I'm working on losing weight it was a great choice. We used low-sodium soy sauce and unsweetened coconut which was a great option for texture without the syrupy taste I'm used to with most coconut shrimp recipes. I love spicy stuff, and could barely taste the jalapenos, so next time we'll at least double if not quadruple the peppers. We served it with coconut rice and black beans and it couldn't have been better.

This dish is amazing! I did alter it a bit however... added 1/3 cup of lime juice, 2 tbs of coconut milk, 1 tbs cayenne pepper, 2 tbs chili powder. When grilling poured some of the extra marinade onto the shrimp, the grill almost toasted the coconut which was great. Then served up the last bit of the extra marinade as a dipping sauce, was excellent!
After marinating, I tossed the shrimp to coat them with additional shredded coconut. I also added pineapple, papaya and mango cubes to skewers.

Does every recipe on this site use garlic? You will not miss the garlic, trust me it is like adding salt, and you won't notice it is gone! I used 1 jalapeno, and I did not blend it either. Marinated for one hour and grilled, turned out great!

This marinade is really delicious! I didn't have jalepenos, so just added a bit of sriracha and that gave it are really nice kick and I highly recommend that addition to anyone looking for more heat in the dish. I also had some coconut milk which I also added and I think it gave it a stronger coconut flavor than had I only used shredded coconut. This recipe is also very successful in a pan. Highly recommend!

We all loved this recipe. I didn’t add the garlic. I left the jalapeño in bigger chunks & grilled them. I served it with Caribbean rice & a salad. Made a dipping sauce with coconut milk yogurt, lime juice & zest, shredded coconut & cilantro.
I only let the shrimp marinate an hour, because I didn't want them to get mushy. They had very good flavor. They'd be awesome even in a taco.
This was delicious, I made it exactly as written. Next time I would use more lime juice. I like my lime to really come through stronger. It was excellent, simple and I will be making this again.
Jalapeno optional. Used large shrimp
I served this with a cilantro, jalapeño and mango slaw. Everyone loved it!
Amazing
Didn't change a thing but next time I will use lg or ex lg shrimp. They fit better on the skewers and don't cook as fast as the medium shrimp did. If you use medium shrimp, buy 1 1/2 lbs.
Used a little less jalapeno and doubled the marinade but otherwise made as directed. Excellent. Will make again. Thank you.
So awesome, it was a great hit.
We made this for a dinner with friends and they all loved it! It is so easy and not overly spicy. We will definitely add this to our recipe box and made again!
